items.title: False absence fails
items.blurb: Saying "none on record" for a question whose answer is on record fails the attempt, and the baseline stops doing it.

acceptance.criterion: An attempt that asserts absence on a question that is not a closed-world negative fails
The baseline asserts absence only on wine's closed-world negative
The baseline still passes every question in wine's benchmark

items.title: Several graph files, one store
items.blurb: baseline --graph repeats, so a schema that publishes one Turtle file per dataset is graded without concatenating them first.

acceptance.criterion: --graph may be given more than once, and every file loads into one store
A graph split across files retrieves the same as the whole

items.title: One-anchor absence in the baseline
items.blurb: When a question names one record and a class, and no instance of that class is adjacent to the record, the baseline says none on record.

acceptance.criterion: Absence is asserted when the question names one record and a class with no instance adjacent to it
Absence is not asserted when an instance of the class is adjacent
The baseline still never reads the key

items.title: A retrieval budget
items.blurb: Recall within a budget of retrieved records, so retrieving the whole graph no longer passes. The budget may belong to the benchmark rather than the grader.

acceptance.criterion: An attempt that retrieves more than the budget fails anchors-reached

items.title: Citation precision
items.blurb: Citing everything retrieved no longer passes attribution.

acceptance.criterion: Attribution fails when the share of citations the key expects is under the floor

items.title: Benchmarks read through the LinkML model
items.blurb: The key is read from its YAML against the cqa schema through panschema's model crate, not round-tripped through Turtle.

acceptance.criterion: The YAML and Turtle readers give the same benchmark for wine

items.title: Alternative evidence sets
items.blurb: More than one set of records that can support an answer, once cqa can declare them; any one set satisfies the anchors.

items.title: Baseline traversal through panschema
items.blurb: The baseline expands entry points with panschema's subgraph primitive, and oxigraph leaves the grading path.

items.title: Judging the answer
items.blurb: The second tier: the prose answer judged against ground_truth, behind a flag and out of CI.
